questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A English speakning country in the EU, to improve my english.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, both UCC and UCPH had good information on there websites. I only missed that there were resticted moduls for visiting students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of emails and a good orientation event. We recived a lot of good information on where to go it your needed any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The host institution helped with it, so it way vey easy. There found the accommodation for me and i only had to register.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In gerneral the rent is very expensive and it can be hard to finde accommodation on your own, because booking already start in February/March. But there is a lot of good student accommodation off campus but close by, and UCC help to finde you a place to stay. There have a accommodation office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Apply for exchange though mobility online, wait for a email for UCC. In the meantime prepar OLA and pre-approval. Registration at UCC though a online application, with good intructions. Got accepted, start to finde accommodation though the university.  Set op UCC acount. Apply for modules.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always contact The International Office by phone or email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had some timetable clashs so it did not turned out as planed, but i was still happy about the result.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It takes time, dont be stressed about it. Some things will happende later than what you expect, but it will turn out fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels was fine comparede to that i both had second, third and fourth year courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was only lectures and laboratory exercises. Only in some curses we were told about textbook and expected to read. There what no overview of the curriculum based on the textbook and I missed the exercises that we have on UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Cell Biology and Biomembranes, The Nervous System, Cell Signalling
Developmental Genetics, Virology, Fundamentals of Microbiology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Virology! It had a very  good lecture/doctor teaching and she used a lot of different teaching methodes; Online lab, physical lab, lecture, movies amongst others.

questions.answer: I could have had a medical expence, but the University have a health center, that helps students to get normal dotor appointments for free.

questions.answer: I used a lot more money on experiences compared to what i expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All the clubs (55 clubs) and societies (>117 societies) you can dream about.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Found the club or society that fits you. I enjoyed the mountaineering. there had inddoor climbing to times a week and a sunday hike.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to west cork!! Rent a car and see The Ring of Beara, Mizenhead, Killarney, Dingel. Take the train to Cobh, se the colorfull city and the musseums and the big church. Cobh is the last place Titanic left from. And see Blarney Castle and Gougane Barra Natrional Forest Park. You can also take som bustrips or join the Mountaineering on there sunday hikes

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and societies! It is very easy in the begining and then look out for activities hostet by the international office at UCC.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The culture was not that differences but the must challeging could be the little oldschool way of doing things - nothing to worry about.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture about the pub, which is a very nice place to meet and there is a nice atmosphere and sometimes music.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Things take time at that is not a bad sign, so stay calm it will all work out fine. 
Join as many social activity as possible. UCC have a lot of clubs and societies. 
Be aware that the exams is written by hand.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Housing is expensive and it can be hard to find it but the University will help you! UCC is a very supporting University there always have someone to help you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new Friends and the big international community. I am very glad that i lived in at student accommodation with shared kitchen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The late relase of timetables and the late premission to take modules.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
